sentences.text: The genus Planicoxa was described by DiCroce and Carpenter in 2001, with the type species Planicoxa venenica named that same year.
The known fossils include a well-preserved ilium, femurs, tibias, vertebrae, and other skeletal material.
While the femurs are typical for ornithopods, the ilium features a short, horizontal postacetabular process that functions as an antitrochanter.
Fossils were discovered in Utah, United States, within the Poison Strip Sandstone Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Grand County.

Estimates for the size of Planicoxa venenica vary; some sources suggest a length of 4.5 meters and a weight of 450 kilograms, while other analyses of remains belonging to at least two individuals estimate a length of 6 meters, a height of 2 meters, and a calculated weight of 900 kilograms.
A second species, P. depressa, was established by Carpenter and Wilson in 2008 for material originally named Camptosaurus depressus by Charles Gilmore in 1909.
The material for P. depressa was collected from the Lakota Formation near Hot Springs, South Dakota, and in 2011 it was reassigned to its own genus, Osmakasaurus.
